note: The two mutants of `core/Scalar.hpp`'s wraparound guard that are decisive **only where assertions are compiled out**, split out of m1-12.json after the first run of 2026-09-23 found them surviving there against an expectation of 'caught'. The reason is worth more than the mutants: the guard has two halves, a call to a non-constexpr function and an ORBSIM_EXPECTS beside it, and **in a Debug build the assert does the marker's job too** -- a failing assert is itself not a constant expression, so the bad literal is refused whether or not the marker is there. The marker's unique contribution is in this tree, where `assert` expands to nothing and it is the only thing left standing between a bad literal and 4,294,967,295. The mirror image is also true, so neither tree tests this code on its own: the run-time mutants in the sibling file survive here, because the assertion they trip does not exist. Run both.

mutants.name: the guard's function is marked constexpr, which is the one change that undoes it
mutants.why: The single most important mutant of the task: it asks whether the not-constexpr-ness is what does the work, and in this tree nothing else can answer.

mutants.name: the subtraction keeps only the run-time half of its guard
mutants.why: Deleting the call while keeping the assertion. In Debug this survives, because the assertion refuses the literal by itself; here it is the whole guard.
